Grain came down from the upland farms on flat-bottomed boats, was ground into flour, and went on by rail to the cities of the coast. When the railway reached the upland directly, the boats stopped coming, and within a decade the mill was a warehouse and then a ruin. The town shrank to the handful of families who worked the bridge and the inn.
